chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ya'qoub bin Yazid, from Safwan bin Yahya, from Abdullah bin Maskan, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Or the male attendants with no carnality' until the end of the verse, so he said: The fool who does not (sexually) approach women.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'non-carnal' (ghayr uli al-irbah) mean in the context of male attendants?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Zurara queries Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) regarding the term 'ghayr uli al-irbah' (non-carnal) in Surah An-Nur. The Imam clarifies that it denotes a man who is free from sexual desire or does not approach women, highlighting a state of natural abstinence rather than mere physical capability. This interpretation underscores the distinction between having the capacity for intimacy and being driven by carnal inclination, a key concept in Shia exegesis of social conduct.
